items.transcript: This Stanford Business School experiment really blew my mind. This professor named Tina Selig gave $5 and two hours to a few different groups in her class. And the task was to go and make as high of a return as possible on that $5. Some of the groups went and took a pretty traditional approach. They went and sort of bartered with the $5. They like bought something and then they traded it. Some of the groups went and just figured out how much money they could make in two hours. So they started like a bike refilling station or they got reservations at a local restaurant that they would then sell. But the winning group thought completely differently about the problem. They looked at what they really had and realized that the $5 that they've been given was a complete distraction. They recognized that the most valuable asset was the presentation time in front of the Stanford students that they were going to be given at the end of the experiment. So they called a bunch of local companies and offered up their presentation slot as an ad for that company. They ended up making $750 for this 15-minute presentation slot, an enormous return.
